_comment: CROSS-REPO WIRE CONTRACT for sub-agent model tiering. The management plane
PRODUCES these two payloads; this runtime CONSUMES them.
STRUCTURE IS NOW ALIGNED with the producer's copy: same top-level
{config_getAgent, config_getModelBinding} envelopes, same casing split, same
already-projected menu. The contract test here reads this structure.
BYTES ARE NOT YET IDENTICAL, and the remaining difference is not an oversight.
The producer's copy uses generated provider names that carry internal
deployment identifiers, and this repository is public — it must not contain
them. So `provider` values here keep the SHAPE of a generated name
(<runtime>-<type>-<qualifier>) with neutral tokens.
That leaves the two files un-`cmp`-able, which is the one thing a shared
fixture exists to prevent. Resolving it needs a decision on the producer side,
not a workaround here:
- neutralise the provider names in the canonical copy (they are sample
values, not contract — the contract is that `provider` is an opaque
string), after which this file can be a byte-for-byte copy; or
- keep the canonical copy internal and treat THIS file as the public
projection, with the producer asserting both.
Until then: structure drift is caught, byte drift is not.
The hash lives OUTSIDE this file — writing it in here would change the bytes
it describes. It is pinned in subagent-tier-wire-contract.test.ts.
NOTE THE CASING SPLIT, deliberate and not a mistake to 'fix':
- the config.getAgent FIELD is snake_case (subagent_model_tiers), matching
every other field of that RPC;
- the menu PAYLOAD inside it is camelCase (whenToUse), matching the
candidate channel and what this runtime parses.
The menu is ALREADY PROJECTED — {revision, items}, not the raw config array.
revision is computed from the stored tier mapping, which only the producer
holds; a second implementation of 'hash the config' would drift into a
permanent false revision_mismatch. This runtime therefore accepts BOTH shapes
on config.getAgent: its own standalone config array, and this envelope.
Every drift here is SILENT. A renamed key errors on neither side: the
normalizer yields nothing, the tool description carries no tiers, `model_tier`
never appears on spawn_subagent, and both suites stay green. That is exactly
how the first integration attempt failed.

_rules: revision is 64 lowercase hex characters (SHA-256), computed over the RAW tier
mapping sorted by tier — NOT over the hydrated candidates. Hashing the
candidates would let one unresolvable model change the revision, which this
runtime would read as a version skew instead of candidate_missing.
Both channels publish the SAME revision for the same configuration.
No tiers is expressed by OMITTING the field, never by an envelope with an
empty list: a revision on one channel with nothing to match on the other is
what the mismatch rule fires on.
The menu never carries provider, modelId, modelConfig or any credential — it
is rendered into a tool description, i.e. into a prompt. The candidates never
`provider` is an OPAQUE string to the consumer. It never parses or pattern-
matches it, which is why neutral sample values here cost nothing semantically.
